head: claude/phase-h-preconditions-retire-consumers
title: consumers: correct every reference naming Streamlit/Android as live [Phase H precondition]
body:
> ⚠️ **DRAFT — Tier 2 by association. Do not merge without an operator OK.** Docs + comments only; **no behaviour change**. The manager owns merges.

## Summary

`BL-20260901-RETIRE-ANDROID-AND-STREAMLIT-FROM-THE-LIVE-FEED`, **part (3)** — the row's own words: *"the one that is easy to skip"*. Every reference in this repo that named the Streamlit dashboard or the Android app as a **live consumer** is corrected. Parts (1) and (2) are in other repos and are handled/blocked separately — see below, stated explicitly rather than left implied.

## Why this is not cosmetic

The row is right about where the staleness sat. `CLAUDE.md` opened its dashboard section with *"consumed by two front-ends"*, and the API table annotated routes with *"Streamlit dashboard"* / *"Android app"* throughout. That is the **field-beats-comment** failure this repo keeps paying for: a session reads the prose, infers a consumer set that no longer exists, and reasons from it — including when deciding whether a route can be gated.

## ⚠️ The correction that is a real defect, not tidying: CORS flipped meaning

Three places carried some form of **"CORS isn't load-bearing"**. That was **true of Streamlit**, whose upstream call was server-side. The Svelte SPA calls **browser-direct** from GitHub Pages, so **CORS is now load-bearing — and a mistake there breaks the only consumer there is.** Corrected in `CLAUDE.md` § CORS, the env-var table, and at the middleware itself in `src/web/api/main.py`, so the next person editing `allow_origins` reads the current rule rather than the retired exemption.

## What changed

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md` § "Dashboard consumer" | Rewritten. Was *"two front-ends"*; now one, with a banner naming the decision and its date. The old **"TWO FRONTENDS REACH THE BOT OVER DIFFERENT TRANSPORTS — do not generalise"** warning is recast as history so it is not read as still live. |
| `CLAUDE.md` architecture diagram | 20 route annotations — `← Streamlit dashboard` / `← Android app` → `← Svelte SPA`. |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL.md` | The frontend/transport table gains a **status** column; the two retired rows are kept for transport archaeology and marked explicitly as *not a consumer set*. |
| `docs/api-tier-policy.md` | *"Today's consumers are … Streamlit … SPA … Android"* → one consumer. **§ 2a (JWT)** said neither consumer *"calls these today"*; corrected to **no consumer has ever called them**, and pointed at Phase H — which is the thing that changes it. |
| `src/web/api/` + `src/core/signal_contract.py` | 16 docstrings/comments that asserted a live-consumer relationship. |

Where a route was *built for* a retired consumer (`/api/bot/performance`, `/ws/market`, `/api/bot/devices/*`), the docstring now says so with the date rather than pretending the route is unowned — the history is why the shape is what it is.

## Architecture impact

- [x] **Architecture docs updated** — `docs/ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL.md` and `docs/api-tier-policy.md` both reflect the single-consumer state. No schema, model-boundary, pipeline-stage or config-shape change; the change *is* the doc correction.

## Test plan

- [x] **442 passed, 6 skipped** — `pytest -k "web_api or bot_web or devices_router or learning or notifications or reports"`.
- [x] `ruff check` clean on all 15 touched Python files.
- [x] `scripts/check_api_tier_policy.py` — OK.
- [x] `scripts/ops/check_backlog_refs.py --base origin/main` — *"every tracking id this change introduces resolves to a filed backlog row"*.
- [x] **The three collection errors are not mine.** `test_main_loop`, `test_exit_loop_wiring`, `test_monitor_ohlcv_fetcher` fail to collect on `ModuleNotFoundError: ccxt`. **Verified by stashing the change and re-running on `main` — identical failure.** Not asserted from plausibility.
- [ ] CI green

⚠️ **On the sandbox:** my brief said pytest was absent and such failures were tooling. **Not accurate** — pytest is present; `fastapi`, `pandas`, `cffi`, `email-validator` were missing. Installed, and the suite was run for real. Flagging it so the next session does not skip validation on the same false premise.

## ⚠️ Scope — the two parts this PR does NOT do, and why

The row's `done_condition` names three things. This PR is **(3)**.

**(1) + (2) for Streamlit — done, in a companion DRAFT PR** on `benbaichmankass/ict-trader-dashboard` (branch `claude/phase-h-preconditions-retire-streamlit`). It moves the 9,628-line `streamlit_app.py` to `archive/streamlit_app_RETIRED_2026-09-01.py` byte-identically and replaces the entry point with a notice page. **Verified by AST, not grep:** the stub's only imports are `__future__` and `streamlit`, and its only URL literals point at the SPA — it *cannot* reach the live feed. Replacing rather than deleting is deliberate: Community Cloud serves the last good build of a deleted file, which would leave a live-looking dashboard still polling the bot.

**(2) for Android — BLOCKED, and this is a real hand-off, not an omission.** `ict-trader-android/CLAUDE.md` carries an explicit operator directive (2026-08-13): 🧊 **ON ICE — do not open speculative work here**, reversible *"only on an explicit operator instruction"*. Adding an archive banner is repo-side work in a frozen repo, so I did not open a PR there. Evidence I *can* offer on part (1) for Android:

- **`device_tokens` has 0 rows on the live host** (unauthenticated read, 2026-09-01). The app's only write to the bot is FCM device registration, so **no device is registered and the push path reaches nobody** — the standing *"push channel is dark"* finding, now doing double duty as retirement evidence.
- I **cannot** prove the app makes no *reads*; a read leaves no queryable trace. So I am not claiming part (1) is demonstrated for Android — only that its write path is provably idle and the operator has twice stated the app is not in use.

⚠️ **One thing the operator may want to know:** the ON-ICE banner (2026-08-13) justifies the freeze with *"The operator is using the web app (**Streamlit** + the Svelte SPA)"*. The 2026-09-01 decision supersedes that. The banner is now internally stale, and correcting it is itself work in the frozen repo — flagged, not done.

## Filed for follow-ups

- **Android repo-side archival** — operator hand-off, per the ON-ICE directive above.
- **Deleting the Streamlit Community Cloud deployment** — operator action at share.streamlit.io; nothing in either repo can do it. Post-merge the deployment redeploys the notice page and reaches no bot data, which satisfies *"no longer calls the live API"*, but the app object still exists.
- **The ON-ICE banner's stale Streamlit justification** in `ict-trader-android/CLAUDE.md`.
